prompt:
Generate one single 16:9 frame from a gritty live-action historical film set in the Caribbean in the 1770s. This is an ENVIRONMENT SHOT: the weather and physical place are the subject. Natural photographic depth, ordinary imperfect exposure, humid surfaces, restrained color, slight organic grain. It must feel like a real place under weather, not a polished concept-art illustration or a tourist brochure. Authentic period materials: rough limewashed masonry, aged timber, wood shingles, small clay tiles, hemp rope, dirt or worn stone, tropical vegetation. No modern roads, concrete infrastructure, electricity poles, cars, engines, steel containers, corrugated sheet metal, rubber tyres, plastic, modern ships, modern roof sheeting, or visible cameras/aircraft. No fantasy castle, no pirate theme park, no oil-painting composition, no orange-and-teal grading, no gold light, no dramatic spotlight beams, no giant lightning bolt, no tornado, no tsunami, no fiery destruction. No caption, writing, logo, watermark graphic, split screen or collage. A continuous plausible space with useful physical details and a specific weather moment. This is a first frame for a restrained 10–12 second cinematic environmental shot; keep moving phenomena at a believable scale rather than frozen gigantic action.

A GROUND-LEVEL OBSERVATIONAL SHOT made from under the dark shelter of a low wooden veranda, at a standing person's chest height with a normal 35mm lens. The camera is dry in the lee of a small house; the top edge includes a rough low eave, and one thick wet timber post cuts into the extreme left foreground, not the center. Beyond shelter, a narrow UNPAVED Caribbean village lane about fifteen meters long runs past rough pale limewashed walls and battered blue-green wooden shutters. The road is mostly mud and shallow rushing water. Heavy gray daylight, wind-driven RAIN moves slantwise from upper right to lower left; water spilling from the near roof falls in broken irregular strands near the edge. Wet banana leaves beyond a small garden wall bend toward the left; loose slender branches scrape the plaster, with natural uneven movement. A single thin roof shingle lies in the gutter. Details are partially blurred by rain and humidity, not digitally over-sharpened. Keep usable visibility of the lane through the rain. No central person, no posed observer, no heroic rescue. One feels the camera operator has stopped under a roof and is simply watching the storm make a familiar lane difficult to cross. Avoid a central vanishing-point postcard, decorative puddle mirrors, quaint clean resort architecture, or rain drawn as a uniform graphic overlay. Deep enough focus to connect shelter, street and distant vegetation. Fixed camera, no camera movement needed.
